newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly lose ground with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly lose ground with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices mostly lost ground Tuesday in lackluster trade, undermined by relatively mild East Coast weather and cratering crude prices amid concerns about renewed Iraqi oil sales, sources said.

"Sellers are trying to hold their numbers, but buyers definitely backed off when they saw crude fall," said one cash trader, noting high sulphurs remained under the most pressure after a recent spate of refinery problems.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to about $22.50 a barrel, with January one percent paper off more than 50 cents with crude to the low-$22 area, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour notionally held steady at $24.50-75 and $23.00-25, respectively.

High sulphurs in NYH again were were on the defensive, with three percent tumbling another 75 cents to $18 or lower. Traders said recent refinery problems like Star's damaged H-oil unit in Louisiana were likely to keep HSFO pressured near-term.

U.S. Gulf Coast one percent eased slightly to $19.50-75, while three percent slid 25-50 cents to the low-$16 area. USG December three percent paper was talked at about $16, with January in the low-$16s, off about 50 cents.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate gas prices tumbled more than 10 cents Tuesday to the $4.05-4.10/mmBtu area, still well-above NYH one percent resid at a $3.57/mmBtu equivalent.
